sources.shortCitation: BnF authority record for Ninon Steinhof
sources.fullCitation: Bibliothèque nationale de France, notice de personne “Steinhof, Ninon”, pseudonyme, forme internationale, FRBNF14700943, ark:/12148/cb14700943p. Female, writing in French and translating from German, described as a translator. The BnF gives the dates as “Naissance : 18..?” and “Mort : 19..”, indicating a nineteenth-century birth and a twentieth-century death, with neither year established. “Steinhoff, Ninon” is recorded as a rejected form. The notice cites two sources: the printed music “Adieu”, music by Pierre Candel, words by Ninon Steinhoff and André Legrand, 1934; and the French adaptation of Ferdinand Bruckner's play “Les criminels”, made with André Mauprey in 1950. ISNI 0000 0001 1982 6820. Sixteen bibliographic records are linked to her as author. Accessed 2 August 2026.

sources.fullCitation: “Valéry e Claudel. Uma conferência no ‘Lycée Français’.” Diário de Notícias (Rio de Janeiro), ano I, no. 36, 17 July 1930, p. 15. media.altText: Black-and-white portrait photograph of Ninon Steinhoff, captioned “Sra. Ninon Steinhof” in Diário de Notícias, Rio de Janeiro, 17 July 1930.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published in Brazil in 1930 and no photographer is credited. Under Brazilian Law No. 9,610/1998, art. 44, copyright in photographic works lasts 70 years from 1 January of the year following first publication; that term has expired. In the United States, works published before 1 January 1931 are in the public domain. The local file is a reduced-resolution crop from the digitized newspaper page.
